newsitem.title: USA: Task force eyed as fishhooks injure two U.S. diners.
newsitem.headline: Task force eyed as fishhooks injure two U.S. diners.

text.p: Tiny fishhooks hidden in the food of salad bars have injured two people and prompted health officials Tuesday to say they may set up a task force with police to investigate.

Doctors performed surgery on a 58-year-old man Sunday to remove a three-pronged fishhook from his small intestine after he swallowed the hook while eating food from a salad bar at a restaurant in Kansas City.
Police later searched the salad bar and found nine more hooks in the lettuce bowl.
The incident was similar to one last month at a different restaurant about 20 miles away in Leavenworth, Kansas. In that case, a woman bit into a fishhook in her salad but did not swallow it.

Clayton Pape, manager of milk and food protection at the Kansas City Health Department, said he was looking at similar food- and drug-tampering episodes from the 1980s to see how authorities handled them.

"There's major concern here -- especially on our part," Pape said. "Law enforcement, local health departments and the Greater Kansas City Restaurant Association need to develop a strategy to minimise the risk of this happening again."
Kansas City police said they were aware of the incident in Leavenworth but had no evidence to connect the two cases.
A spokesman for the Greater Kansas City Restaurant Association was not immediately available to comment.
